title.narrative: UNDP Support to Justice Sector and Police Reform BGD

description.narrative:
Bangladeshs recent political transitions and social unrest have exposed significant challenges in the justice and police sectors, highlighting an urgent need for reform. A successful political transition depends on the demonstrated will to tackle reform challenges and work towards resolution of deeply rooted institutional problems to build back public trust. Bangladeshs rätts- och brottsbekämpningssystem står inför utmaningar som har sina rötter i politisering, korruption och begränsad institutionell kapacitet. Polisen och rättsväsendet arbetar med att ta fram en reformagenda. Kommissioner har inrättats med korta mandat för att utarbeta rekommendationer om dessa systemfrågor och föreslå genomförbara reformer. Den begränsade tidsram som de har fått och bristen på mekanismer för kontinuitet utgör dock en risk för hållbarheten i deras rekommendationer. Det föreslagna bidraget syftar till att stötta reformkommissionerna inom polis och rättsväsen i arbetet att ta fram effektiva reformrekommendationer inom ramen för sina mandat och samtidigt bygga upp mekanismer för att säkerställa kontinuitet efter det att de har underställts interimsregeringen.

Bangladesh’s justice and law enforcement systems face challenges rooted in politicization, corruption, and limited institutional capacity. The police and the judiciary are working on developing a reform agenda. The JRC and PRC have been established with short mandates to develop recommendations regarding these systemic issues and to propose actionable reforms. However, the limited time-frame that they have been given and lack of continuity mechanisms pose risks to the sustainability of their recommendations. The proposed contribution aims to empower the Justice sector reform- and Police reform Commissions to deliver effective and sustainable reform recommendations within their mandates while building mechanisms to ensure continuity beyond submission to the Interim Government.

sector.narrative: Justice, law and order policy, planning and administration

description.narrative:
The project has made important contributions to justice sector reform in Bangladesh, supporting both institutional change and broadbased stakeholder engagement during a period of political transition.
Strengthening Judicial Independence and Governance: The programme has played a central role in advancing reforms aimed at judicial selfadministration, transparent judicial appointments, and a more independent justice system. With programme support, several key pieces of legislation have been adopted, including laws on the Judicial Secretariat, Supreme Court appointments, legal aid, and commercial courts. These reforms represent important steps toward strengthening judicial governance and reducing executive influence over the justice system.
Supporting the Supreme Courts Reform Agenda: In response to the 2024 public demand for justice, accountability, and protection from arbitrary use of power, the programme has supported the Supreme Courts justice reform agenda and facilitated broad stakeholder engagement.
Nine judicial reform discussions were organised across Chattogram, Rajshahi, Mymensingh, Rangpur, Sylhet, Khulna, Barisal, and Dhaka, bringing together judges, advocates, and other justice sector actors to debate the need for judicial independence directly with the Chief Justice.The outcomes of these discussions were presented at the National Justice Conference to the head of government and directly informed revisions to the Supreme Court Strategic Plan. Despite political transition and the repeal of some reform measures, these dialogues helped sustain momentum for justice sector reform and demonstrated continued demand for judicial independence among key stakeholders. Approximately 1,000 justice sector officials and stakeholders participated in total.
Supporting National Reform Commissions: The programme has provided targeted assistance to both the Judicial Reform Commission and the Police Reform Commission. This support included eight stakeholder consultations on police and justice reform, logistical and coordination assistance, and expert advisory papers on judicial independence, prosecution reform, model police stations, and peoplecentred policing. Findings from the Commissions reports subsequently shaped policy recommendations of the Interim Government and political parties through the work of the Consensus Commission, demonstrating the programmes influence on national policy dialogue.
Advancing Prosecution Reform: The programme has helped advance discussions on transforming the Attorney Generals Office into a professional prosecution service. Engagement with young people and future legal professionals has contributed to building awareness and support for a modernised, independent prosecution system.
Building Future Reform Capacity: A Young Professionals/Internship Programme was established to strengthen legal research and policy capacity among emerging professionals. Two cohorts of 25 interns from leading universities have participated, gaining direct exposure to justice sector reform processes and contributing to policy research.
Initiating Judicial Digitalisation and Commercial Court Establishment: The programme has initiated foundational work for the establishment of commercial courts and judicial digitalisation, with operationalisation planned from 2026. A comprehensive stateofplay assessment on judicial digitalisation has been completed, and policy recommendations have been provided to the Supreme Court to guide future implementation.
